latest_release.body:
### RubyGems

#### Enhancements:

* Installs bundler 4.1.1 as a default gem.

#### Bug fixes:

* Fix file permissions during gem extraction. Pull request [#10128](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10128) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Resolve chained symlink targets before creating them during extraction. Pull request [#10119](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10119) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Keep negative any terms when PubGrub resolves conflicts. Pull request [#10112](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10112) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Serialize concurrent installs of the same gem. Pull request [#10107](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10107) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Keep resolved prereleases when sorting install requests. Pull request [#10100](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10100) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Forward keyword arguments in the IPv4 fallback TCPSocket#initialize. Pull request [#10098](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10098) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Push attestations with non-ASCII bytes on Ruby 3.2 and 3.3. Pull request [#10097](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10097) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Gem::YAMLSerializer::Parser only reads the first document of a YAML stream. Pull request [#10088](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10088) by Ben Sheldon and Hiroshi SHIBATA

### Bundler

#### Bug fixes:

* Assign the specs missing from the shard list to shard_d. Pull request [#10127](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10127) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Require a digest on every content-addressed row of a checksummed lockfile. Pull request [#10122](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10122) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Keep frozen installs to gems the lockfile covers for content-addressed rows. Pull request [#10120](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10120) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Stop shipping the URI and YAML serializer entry files in the Bundler gem. Pull request [#10113](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10113) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Keep negative any terms when PubGrub resolves conflicts. Pull request [#10112](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10112) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Check gem requirements when locking from legacy indexes. Pull request [#10111](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10111) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Retry resolution with transitive prereleases. Pull request [#10110](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10110) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Explain activation conflicts caused by a Gemfile require. Pull request [#10109](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10109) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Allow full updates to downgrade a yanked gem. Pull request [#10106](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10106) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Honor `--prefer-local` when locking platform variants. Pull request [#10108](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10108) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Honor `--jobs` when installing from `vendor/cache`. Pull request [#10102](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10102) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Allow `bundle lock --add-platform` to add native platforms from JRuby. Pull request [#10105](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10105) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Show fourth-segment and prerelease updates in `bundle outdated --filter-patch`. Pull request [#10103](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10103) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Preserve inline settings after a forked install. Pull request [#10099](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10099) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Resolve dependencies before `bundle add` updates the Gemfile. Pull request [#10101](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10101) by Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Keep mirror settings readable by Bundler 4.0. Pull request [#10075](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10075) by Paul Wille
* Fix Gem::URI redefinition warnings on older RubyGems. Pull request [#10074](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10074) by Paul Wille and Hiroshi SHIBATA
* Read plugin index sections that are not hashes as empty. Pull request [#10076](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/pull/10076) by Hiroshi SHIBATA

detail.readme:
# RubyGems

RubyGems is a package management framework for Ruby.

A package (also known as a library) contains a set of functionality that can be invoked by a Ruby program, such as reading and parsing an XML file.
We call these packages "gems" and RubyGems is a tool to install, create, manage and load these packages in your Ruby environment.

RubyGems is also a client for [RubyGems.org](https://rubygems.org), a public repository of Gems that allows you to publish a Gem
that can be shared and used by other developers. See our guide on publishing a Gem at [guides.rubygems.org](https://guides.rubygems.org/publishing/)

## Getting Started

Installing and managing a Gem is done through the `gem` command. To install a Gem such as [Faraday][faraday]:

```bash
gem install faraday
```

[faraday]: https://github.com/lostisland/faraday?tab=readme-ov-file

RubyGems will download the Faraday Gem from RubyGems.org and install it into your Ruby environment.

Finally, inside your Ruby program, load the Faraday gem and start hacking:

```ruby
require 'faraday'
response = Faraday.get('https://rubygems.org')
# do something with `response`...
```

For more information about how to use RubyGems, see our RubyGems basics guide at [guides.rubygems.org](https://guides.rubygems.org/rubygems-basics/)

## Bundler

Bundler makes sure Ruby applications run the same code on every machine. It is developed in this repository and ships with Ruby.

It does this by managing the gems that the application depends on. Given a list of gems, it can automatically download and install those gems, as well as any other gems needed by the gems that are listed. Before installing gems, it checks the versions of every gem to make sure that they are compatible, and can all be loaded at the same time. After the gems have been installed, Bundler can help you update some or all of them when new versions become available. Finally, it records the exact versions that have been installed, so that others can install the exact same gems.

For example, these commands will allow you to use Bundler to manage the `rspec` gem for your application:

```bash
bundle init
bundle add rspec
bundle install
bundle exec rspec
```

For more information about how to use Bundler, see the guides at [guides.rubygems.org](https://guides.rubygems.org/)

## Requirements

* RubyGems supports Ruby 3.0 or later.

## Installation

RubyGems is already installed in your Ruby environment, you can check the version you have installed by running `gem --version` in your terminal emulator.

In some cases Ruby & RubyGems may be provided as OS packages. This is not a
recommended way to use Ruby & RubyGems. It's better to use a Ruby Version
Manager, such as [rbenv](https://github.com/rbenv/rbenv) or
[chruby](https://github.com/postmodern/chruby). If you still want to use the
version provided by your OS package manager, please also use your OS package
manager to upgrade rubygems, and disregard any other installation instructions
given below.

If you would like to manually install RubyGems:

* Download from https://rubygems.org/pages/download, unpack, and `cd` into RubyGems' src
* OR clone this repository and `cd` into the repository

Install RubyGems by running:

    $ ruby setup.rb

For more details and other options, see:

    $ ruby setup.rb --help

## Upgrading RubyGems

To upgrade to the latest RubyGems, run:

    $ gem update --system

See [UPGRADING](doc/UPGRADING.md) for more details and alternative instructions.

## Release policy

RubyGems and Bundler share a version number and are released together.

The release policy is somewhat similar to the release policy of Ruby itself:

* Frequent patch releases (every 2-4 weeks) including bug fixes, minor
  enhancements, small features, or even medium sized features declared as
  experimental for battle testing.
* Yearly minor releases including bigger features, and minor breaking changes
  (affecting only edge cases and a very small set of users).
* Occasional major releases (replacing yearly minors) including major breaking
  changes.

## Documentation

RubyGems uses [rdoc](https://github.com/rdoc/rdoc) for documentation. A compiled set of the docs
can be viewed online at [docs.ruby-lang.org](https://docs.ruby-lang.org/en/master/Gem.html).

RubyGems also provides a comprehensive set of guides which covers numerous topics such as
creating a new gem, security practices and other resources at https://guides.rubygems.org

## Getting Help

### Filing Tickets

Got a bug and you're not sure?  You're sure you have a bug, but don't know
what to do next?  In any case, let us know about it!  The best place
for letting the RubyGems team know about bugs or problems you're having is
[on the RubyGems issues page at GitHub](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/issues).

### Bundler Compatibility

See https://guides.rubygems.org/bundler-compatibility/ for known issues.

### Supporting

RubyGems is a community project. Please consider sponsoring [individual contributors for their great OSS
work](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/graphs/contributors).

In addition, Ruby Central administers grant-funded work for improvements to `ruby/rubygems`, as well as running
RubyGems.org (the service). You can support Ruby Central by attending or [sponsoring](mailto:sponsors@rubycentral.org)
a [RubyConf](https://rubyconf.org/), or by [joining as a supporting member](https://rubycentral.org/#/portal/signup).

### Contributing

If you'd like to contribute to RubyGems, that's awesome, and we <3 you. Check out our [guide to contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information.

### Code of Conduct

Everyone interacting in the RubyGems project’s codebases, issue trackers, chat rooms, and mailing lists is expected to follow the [contributor code of conduct](https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/blob/master/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
